summary: An 18,064-to-19,500-seat arena for the Golden State Warriors (NBA) and Golden State Valkyries (WNBA, since 2025), anchoring an 11-acre, privately financed mixed-use development in Mission Bay with 580,000 sq ft of office/lab space (leased in full by Uber as its San Francisco headquarters since 2022), 100,000 sq ft of retail ("Thrive City") and a 35,000 sq ft public plaza; designed by MANICA Architecture with Gensler (interiors), built by a Mortenson/Clark Construction joint venture, and opened September 6, 2019.

milestones.text: Golden State Warriors ownership purchases the ~12-acre former Salesforce.com site in Mission Bay
Chase Center opens; the Warriors begin play there
Chase Center achieves LEED Gold certification (Building Design and Construction: New Construction), one of few major US sports venues to do so
Uber occupies the adjacent Mission Bay 3 & 4 office towers (1655 & 1725 3rd St) as its San Francisco/global headquarters, on a 20-year lease covering ~584,000-586,000 sq ft for ~4,000 employees

SF Board of Supervisors approves a separate, Warriors-proposed hotel/condo/retail complex (129-room hotel, 21 condos, ~25,000 sf retail) on adjacent Blocks 29-30 near Chase Center; as of the most recent reporting found (~Feb 2025), construction had not begun. Its relationship to this parcel (8722025) is not confirmed -- see open questions
Golden State Valkyries (WNBA expansion team) play their inaugural regular-season home game at Chase Center, vs. the Los Angeles Sparks

open_questions: Chase Center's final cost is genuinely disputed in reporting: $1.4B is the most-repeated figure (Construction Dive), but a Warriors executive (Rick Welts, per Wikipedia) put the actual final cost closer to $1.3B after a roughly 30% overrun from an original budget. A separate 2019 Construction Dive piece on the (distinct, unbuilt) hotel/condo proposal used '$1.5B Chase Center' in its own headline, which appears to conflate the arena with that proposal; that figure is not used here.
Uber's exact current headcount or lease status as of 2026 was not independently verified; the source describing its 584,000-586,000 sq ft lease is from January 2022.

The Warriors-proposed hotel/condo/retail complex on adjacent Blocks 29-30 is financially and physically tied to Chase Center but may sit on a separate parcel; whether it falls within blklot 8722025 or is a distinct, not-yet-built record is not confirmed. Current 2026 construction status is also unconfirmed.

No primary Port of San Francisco or OCII page dedicated specifically to Chase Center was found (as a privately financed project, it may not have one); the only agency-level source found was SFPUC/CleanPowerSF's sustainability write-up.
